Package paint.shared.utils

Class SharedSquareUtils

java.lang.Object
paint.shared.utils.SharedSquareUtils
public final class SharedSquareUtils extends Object
Utility class providing methods for filtering and evaluating square regions in PAINT recordings. Supports both spatial filtering of track coordinates and multi-criteria visibility selection of squares.

    • filterTracksInSquare

      public static tech.tablesaw.api.Table filterTracksInSquare(tech.tablesaw.api.Table tracks, Square square, int lastRowCol)
      Filters track coordinates to include only those within the specified square.

      This method handles inclusive or exclusive boundaries depending on whether the square is in the last column or row. It operates on a Tablesaw table containing at least TRACK_X_LOCATION and TRACK_Y_LOCATION columns.

      Parameters:
      tracks - table of track data with X/Y coordinate columns
      square - the square region defining coordinate boundaries
      lastRowCol - index of the last row/column in the grid (for boundary handling)
      Returns:
      new Table containing only the tracks located within the specified square

    • applyVisibilityFilterOnRecording

      public static void applyVisibilityFilterOnRecording(List<Square> squares, String recordingName, double minRequiredDensityRatio, double maxAllowableVariability, double minRequiredRSquared, String neighbourMode)
      Applies the full visibility filter to squares belonging to a specific recording.

      The method performs a two-stage filtering process:

      1. Numeric filter

      A square becomes visible if all of the following are true:
      • its R² value is not NaN and ≥ minRequiredRSquared
      • its density ratio ≥ minRequiredDensityRatio
      • its variability ≤ maxAllowableVariability
      If recordingName is non-null, only squares whose getRecordingName() matches the given name are evaluated; others are skipped.

      2. Neighbour filter

      Applied only when neighbourMode is not "Free". A square that passed the numeric filter will remain visible only if it has at least one other visible neighbouring square. Neighbourhood rules:
      • "Relaxed": any of the 8 surrounding squares (edge or corner) counts as neighbouring
      • "Strict": only 4-connected neighbours (up, down, left, right) count
      If neighbourMode is neither "Free", "Relaxed", nor "Strict", an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

      Final step

      Any square not selected during the neighbour filter is set to invisible.
      Parameters:
      squares - the squares to filter
      recordingName - if non-null, only squares from this recording are evaluated; if null, all squares are processed
      minRequiredDensityRatio - minimum density ratio required to be visible
      maxAllowableVariability - maximum variability allowed to be visible
      minRequiredRSquared - minimum R² required to be visible
      neighbourMode - neighbour rule: "Free", "Relaxed", or "Strict"

    • applyVisibilityFilter

      public static void applyVisibilityFilter(List<Square> squares, double minDensityRatio, double maxVariability, double minRSquared, String neighbourMode)
      Applies the visibility filter to all squares in a recording using the given numeric thresholds and neighbour-mode rules.

      This is a convenience method that delegates to applyVisibilityFilterOnRecording(List, String, double, double, double, String) without restricting to a specific recording name (i.e., it applies the filter to all squares in the list).

      Filtering steps

      1. Numeric filter: A square becomes visible if:
        • its R² is not NaN and ≥ minRSquared
        • its density ratio ≥ minDensityRatio
        • its variability ≤ maxVariability
      2. Neighbour filter: Only applied when neighbourMode is not "Free".
        • "Relaxed" → any touching neighbour (8-connected)
        • "Strict" → edge-adjacent neighbour only (4-connected)
      Parameters:
      squares - the list of squares to filter
      minDensityRatio - minimum required density ratio
      maxVariability - maximum allowable variability
      minRSquared - minimum required R²
      neighbourMode - neighbour filtering mode: "Free", "Relaxed", or "Strict"

    • calculateDensity

      public static double calculateDensity(int nrTracks, double area, double time, double concentration)
      Calculates the density of tracks in a specified area over time and considering a concentration factor.

      The density is computed as the number of tracks divided by the area, then divided by the time, and finally divided by the concentration. If any of the area, time, or concentration values are non-positive, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

      Parameters:
      nrTracks - The total number of tracks to calculate density for.
      area - The area over which the density is calculated. Must be positive.
      time - The time period over which the density is calculated. Must be positive.
      concentration - The concentration factor to apply to the density calculation. Must be positive.
      Returns:
      The calculated density as a double.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if area, time, or concentration is less than or equal to zero.
